title: NY State Senate · District 29
area: East Harlem in Manhattan and the South Bronx, including Mott Haven, Port Morris, and Melrose.

context.text: Uncontested general election: incumbent Jose M. Serrano (D, Working Families Party) defeated Nicholas Reyes 69.2%-30.0% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. No Republican or other-party candidate filed for the November 3 general election, so Serrano is unopposed on the ballot.

candidates.name: Jose M. Serrano
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary; unopposed in the general election
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 29 (since 2013); previously District 28 (2005-2013)

summary.text: Jose M. Serrano is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent running unopposed for re-election to NY Senate District 29, covering East Harlem and the South Bronx. First elected to the Senate in 2004, he chairs the Cultural Affairs, Tourism, Parks and Recreation Committee and has served as chair of the Senate Democratic Conference.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in government from Manhattan College.
Served on Community Board 4 and as a New York City Council member for District 17 in the Bronx from 2001 to 2004 before winning election to the State Senate.
Represented Senate District 28 from 2005 to 2013 before redistricting; has represented District 29 since 2013.
Has served as chair of the Senate Democratic Conference.

priorities.text: Healthcare access in the South Bronx, including securing funding for new medical infrastructure at local hospitals.
Environmental and climate legislation, reflected in a top-10% ranking on the Environmental Advocates New York 2026 scorecard.
Cultural affairs, tourism, parks and recreation, as chair of the relevant Senate committee.

positions.summary: Scored 95 (top 10%) on the Environmental Advocates New York 2026 legislative scorecard, which tracks votes on climate, clean water, and toxic-chemical bills.
positions.quote: He looks forward to continuing his environmental work with his colleagues in government and advocates to create a cleaner, healthier, and safer New York.

positions.summary: Helped secure roughly $1 million toward a new cardiac catheterization laboratory at Lincoln Hospital in the Bronx to address healthcare disparities for high-risk South Bronx patients.

record.text: Helped secure about $1 million toward a new cardiac catheterization laboratory at Lincoln Hospital in the Bronx, alongside other federal, state, and local officials and the Governor's office.
Scored 95 out of 100 (top 10% of legislators) on the Environmental Advocates New York 2026 legislative scorecard.

Chairs the Senate Cultural Affairs, Tourism, Parks and Recreation Committee in the 2025-2026 session; also sits on the Aging, Libraries, Women's Issues, Environmental Conservation, Social Services, and Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs committees.

researchNotes: Serrano faces no opponent on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot; his Democratic primary opponent Nicholas Reyes is not included per the research standard. Serrano has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and has no separate campaign website distinct from his official Senate page, so priorities are drawn from official committee assignments and NYSenate.gov press coverage rather than campaign materials; positions beyond climate and healthcare could not be documented with a direct citable statement.
